title: A Fully Analog Continuous-Time CIM Neural ODE Solver for Flow-Matching-Based Fluid Dynamics Generation
evidence_span: The paper proposes a flow-matching MLP-Mixer plus a fully analog continuous-time RRAM CIM neural ODE solver, with noise-aware training and decoder retraining. On three turbulent-flow datasets it reports comparable velocity-field accuracy and 98.24% lower energy and 99.99% lower latency than an NVIDIA A100 while maintaining fidelity under RRAM read/write noise.
problem: Iterative von Neumann computational-fluid-dynamics pipelines impose high latency and energy cost for generating fluid-dynamics fields, while analog CIM must tolerate device noise.
method_or_artifact: Flow-matching MLP-Mixer co-designed with a fully analog continuous-time RRAM compute-in-memory neural ODE solver; noise-aware training and decoder retraining address RRAM read/write noise.
workload_or_benchmark: Turbulent-flow generation on three turbulent-flow datasets; velocity-field accuracy and generation fidelity are compared with convolutional and attention-based flow-matching models.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Analog RRAM CIM with realistic read/write noise; comparison against an NVIDIA A100 GPU. Device, array, ADC/DAC, precision, and fabrication assumptions are not exposed in the public description.
metrics: velocity-field accuracy comparable to convolutional and attention-based models
stable generation fidelity under RRAM read/write noise
limits: The official description does not expose RRAM device parameters, array dimensions, conversion overhead, numerical precision, training cost, or dataset-by-dataset error values; the A100 comparison is not independently verified.

title: Seeing the Unseen: Reverse Engineering Hidden PMU Events by Differential Analysis and Simulation Validation
evidence_span: The paper presents a reverse-engineering framework for hidden performance-monitoring-unit events, reveals branch-related microarchitectural behavior and a hidden UMask-combination pattern on Intel CPUs, and uses the findings for a PMU covert channel for Spectre-v1 in SGX and high-precision website fingerprinting under resource constraints.
problem: Hidden PMU events have been disclosed without their microarchitectural semantics, limiting legitimate use and obscuring their security implications.
method_or_artifact: Differential analysis and simulation validation framework for inferring hidden PMU event semantics, followed by a PMU-based covert-channel demonstration.
workload_or_benchmark: Branch-related PMU events on Intel CPUs; Spectre-v1 in SGX and resource-constrained website fingerprinting as security demonstrations.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Intel processor PMUs, SGX, and Spectre-v1 threat conditions; processor model, counter configuration, noise controls, and attacker capabilities are not specified in the public description.
baselines: previously disclosed hidden PMU events and semantics
metrics: high-precision website fingerprinting (numeric precision not reported)
limits: The description does not report numerical fingerprinting precision, trace counts, attack time, processor generations, simulation fidelity, or mitigation evaluation; it demonstrates a security case rather than establishing generality across CPUs.

title: Fast Template Matching for Quantum Circuits Using Hypergraph
evidence_span: The paper replaces DAG-based quantum-circuit template matching with a commutativity-aware hypergraph that collapses commuting gates while retaining local connectivity. On random and arithmetic benchmarks it reports 11–606x speedup over the DAG implementation in Qiskit while maintaining the same optimization quality.
problem: DAG-based quantum template matching handles gate commutativity but loses local circuit connectivity, causing high matching complexity.
method_or_artifact: Hypergraph representation with commutativity-aware super-nodes and local incremental matching updates limited to the immediate neighborhood.
workload_or_benchmark: Random and arithmetic quantum-circuit benchmarks; comparison against the Qiskit DAG-based implementation.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Quantum-circuit compilation and optimization; gate-set, circuit-size distribution, hardware coupling constraints, and downstream execution assumptions are not reported in the public description.
metrics: same optimization quality as the baseline
limits: The description does not provide circuit counts, gate-set details, absolute runtimes, memory use, or hardware-aware compilation impact; the speedup range requires paper-level distribution and reproducibility checks.

title: OpenSUN: An Open Platform for Exploring Scale-Up Network Systems
evidence_span: OpenSUN is an FPGA-based multi-node, open platform for scale-up systems with accessible I/O controllers, switches, protocol stacks, and software layers. It targets cross-stack exploration of CXL, UALink, NVLink, Unified-Bus-like interconnects, topologies, switch architectures, and system software.
problem: Academic researchers lack an open hardware-based platform for cross-stack experimentation with next-generation scale-up interconnect systems despite commercial solutions.
method_or_artifact: Customizable FPGA-based multi-node platform exposing full-stack I/O controllers, switches, protocol stacks, and software through user-facing interfaces.
workload_or_benchmark: Scale-up network-system prototyping across protocols, topologies, switch/controller architectures, and system-level software; no quantitative benchmark is reported in the public description.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: FPGA-based multi-node implementation with load/store interconnects and shared-memory scale-up semantics; exact FPGA, link, protocol, node-count, and software-stack configurations are not disclosed.
baselines: commercial scale-up interconnect solutions (contextual, not a measured baseline)
metrics: platform component coverage and configurability (numeric evaluation not reported)
limits: The public description establishes an artifact and intended research scope but does not report throughput, latency, resource cost, protocol compliance, node scale, or comparative experiments.

title: KEEP: A KV-Cache-Centric Memory Management System for Efficient Embodied Planning
evidence_span: KEEP manages embodied-planning memory with Static-Dynamic Memory Construction, Multi-hop Memory Re-computation, and Layer-balanced Memory Loading. The components group memory by update frequency, recover important cross-group interactions, and remove layer-imbalance overhead during KV recomputation.
problem: Embodied-planning systems suffer cache invalidation and unbalanced KV loading/computation when memory updates at different rates and cross-attention spans groups.
method_or_artifact: KV-cache-centric memory-management system combining update-frequency-aware granularity, iterative memory-importance propagation for multi-hop recomputation, and layer-balanced loading scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: Embodied planning with dynamic memory updates and KV-cache recomputation; model suite, hardware platform, and quantitative benchmark conditions are not reported in the public description.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Layered KV-cache storage and computation for embodied-planning models; memory hierarchy, accelerator, sequence lengths, and recomputation cost model are unspecified.
baselines: conventional KV-cache management and recomputation strategies (not named in the description)
metrics: reduced cache invalidation (numeric result not reported)
reduced cross-group recomputation impact (numeric result not reported)
reduced layer-imbalance overhead (numeric result not reported)
limits: The description omits model/task suite, latency and memory metrics, baseline implementation, hardware, and accuracy or planning-quality effects; conclusions remain mechanism-level until the paper is reviewed.
